data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure because it replaces 'redundancy of instance' with 'diversity of failure domains', preventing a single-plane configuration error from becoming a global event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single 'industry standard' library or protocol (the 'Common Library Trap'), creating a hidden logical monolith.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of maintaining diverse implementations leads to critical security debt (unpatched vulnerabilities) that provides a common attack vector.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Operational diversity (different deployment pipelines, operators, and environments) ensures that the 'blast radius' of any single administrative or logical error is bounded, whereas a large service's internal redundancy often shares a common orchestration plane (the 'Complexity Paradox'), creating a single point of failure for the entire system.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
